topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the administrative opening, course framing, and lecture learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic, cellular, and architectural basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental biological nature of cancer as a multi-step accumulation of alterations resulting in the breakdown of normal tissue architecture and cellular differentiation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and histopathology of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how local tissue invasion through the basement membrane and secondary metastatic spread define malignancy and distinguish malignant tumors from benign lesions.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical pathophysiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the conventions for naming tumors alongside the pathological mechanisms by which both benign and malignant growths cause morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor incidence in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical symptoms and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address clinical presentation and the diagnostic utility, histology, and limitations of screening programs for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks, reminders regarding practicals, and lecture closing framing.
